# captured 2026-09-22
# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/railway
# args: 
Manage project volumes

Usage: railway volume [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list    List volumes [aliases: ls]
  add     Add a new volume [aliases: create, new]
  delete  Delete a volume [aliases: remove, rm]
  update  Update a volume [aliases: edit, rename]
  detach  Detach a volume from a service
  files   Manage files in a volume [aliases: file]
  browse  Browse files in a volume interactively [aliases: browser]
  attach  Attach a volume to a service
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -s, --service <SERVICE>          Service ID
  -e, --environment <ENVIRONMENT>  Environment ID
  -p, --project <PROJECT_ID>       Project ID to use (defaults to linked project)
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version

Examples:

  railway volume list --json
  railway volume add --service api --mount-path /data --json
  railway volume update --volume volume-id --name data --json
  railway volume delete --volume data --yes --json
  railway volume browse /
  railway volume files list / --json
  railway volume files browse /
  railway volume files download /backup.tar ./backup.tar --json
  railway volume files upload ./backup.tar /backup.tar --json
  railway volume files delete /backup.tar --yes --json
  railway volume files rename /backup.tar /backup-old.tar --json

Aliases:
  list: ls
  add: create, new
  delete: remove, rm
  update: edit, rename
  browse: browser

Automation notes:
  Mount paths must start with `/`. Use volume IDs from `railway volume list --json` when names may collide.
  Downloads fail if LOCAL_PATH exists unless --overwrite or --override is passed. Uploads fail if REMOTE_PATH exists unless --overwrite is passed. Use --json for machine-readable file operation details.
